data.narrative:
QuantumScape is a public Climate & Energy company founded by Jagdeep Singh, Tim Holme, and Fritz Prinz, currently trading at a $3.63B valuation after raising $2B+. The comparable universe consists of 3 same-sector, same-stage peers: Enovix ($1.0B), Solid Power ($504M), and LanzaTech ($73M).

The peer-median method, the sole applicable triangulation approach given available data, yields $504M based on the median valuation across these three public companies. This method reflects the dispersion within the comp set: a range of $73M to $1.0B, with LanzaTech at the low end and Enovix anchoring the upper bound. The $504M implied valuation reflects neither the most speculative nor the most mature comparables in this cohort.

The single-method analysis supports a valuation range of $428M to $580M (median $504M), derived from the peer-median result with standard tolerance bands. However, the current market price of $3.63B implies a substantial premium to this comp-derived range—approximately 7.2x the median estimate. Key uncertainties limiting confidence in the peer-based approach include the narrow comp set of only 3 companies and significant heterogeneity within that set (13.7x spread between min and max). Additional triangulation methods would strengthen conviction; as currently constrained by available data, this analysis represents a lower-bound perspective relative to current market valuation.
